posts.text: “He speaks louder in death.” Rev. Wheeler Parker Jr. remembers his cousin, Emmett Till, who would have turned 85 this month, had he not been murdered. Rev. Parker was with Till the night he was abducted. “It’s an ugly story, but it’s American history,” he tells me. “You should know the truth and the truth will make you free.”

posts.text: A new exhibition imagines what if Emmett Till had lived. Its curator Sarah Lewis tells me it’s intended “to celebrate his unlived life,” noting that “it’s impossible to understand American history and the catalyst for the civil rights movement without engaging with the history and life of Emmett Till.”

As temperatures rise, “America is making a concerted effort to make the problem worse as fast as it possibly can,” argues environmentalist Bill McKibben.

“We've shut down wind farms that are 90% finished off the Atlantic seaboard, put the federal land off-limits to solar panels, done every possible thing we could to buck up 18th century energy technology.”
